# Physics: Semester 1 Learning Project

A complete, shareable learning project for 11th grade physics covering **Kinematics, Projectile Motion, Newton's Laws, Momentum, and Work & Energy**, aligned to the [CA NGSS](https://www.cde.ca.gov/pd/ca/sc/ngssstandards.asp).

Each unit has a unit guide (key concepts, objectives, assessment criteria, practice problems, labs, resources, real-world applications), Cornell notes, and a quiz built from the questions students most often miss.

## Start here

- **Students:** open `index.html` in a browser for the interactive notes, quizzes, and progress checklist. Progress is saved in that browser only.
- **Instructors:** read the outline below, then [docs/assessment.md](docs/assessment.md) and [docs/standards-alignment.md](docs/standards-alignment.md).
- To share the interactive pages by link, turn on GitHub Pages for this repository (Settings → Pages → deploy from the main branch, root folder).

## Semester checklist

### Unit 1: Kinematics (Weeks 1–4)

*How can we describe and predict where an object will be and how fast it will be moving?*

**Key concepts:** position, distance, displacement; speed and velocity; acceleration; motion graphs; kinematic equations; free fall.

**Objectives**

- [ ] **K1** Distinguish distance from displacement and speed from velocity, and calculate each from a description of motion.
- [ ] **K2** Calculate acceleration and explain what its sign means for an object's motion.
- [ ] **K3** Read and sketch position–time and velocity–time graphs, using slope and area to find velocity, acceleration, and displacement.
- [ ] **K4** Choose and solve the right kinematic equation for a constant-acceleration problem, showing knowns, unknowns, and units.
- [ ] **K5** Solve free-fall problems and explain why mass does not affect the acceleration of a falling object.

**Checkpoints**

- [ ] Cornell notes complete; every cue answered aloud with the Notes column covered
- [ ] Most-missed quiz at 80% or higher
- [ ] Practice problems completed and checked
- [ ] Lab completed and written up (claim, evidence, reasoning)
- [ ] IXL skills at SmartScore 80+

### Unit 2: Projectile Motion (Weeks 5–7)

*Why does a thrown object follow a curved path, and how can we predict where it will land?*

**Key concepts:** vector components; independence of motion; horizontal motion; vertical motion; trajectory; range and launch angle.

**Objectives**

- [ ] **P1** Resolve a velocity vector into horizontal and vertical components and recombine components into a resultant.
- [ ] **P2** Explain why the horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile are independent, using evidence from a demonstration or simulation.
- [ ] **P3** Solve horizontally launched projectile problems for time of flight, range, and impact velocity.
- [ ] **P4** Solve angled-launch problems on level ground for time of flight, maximum height, and range.
- [ ] **P5** Predict how changing launch speed, angle, or height changes a projectile's path.

**Checkpoints**

- [ ] Cornell notes complete; every cue answered aloud with the Notes column covered
- [ ] Most-missed quiz at 80% or higher
- [ ] Practice problems completed and checked
- [ ] Lab completed and written up (claim, evidence, reasoning)
- [ ] IXL skills at SmartScore 80+

### Unit 3: Newton's Laws (Weeks 8–11)

*What makes an object's motion change, and how can we predict the change?*

**Key concepts:** force and net force; free-body diagrams; first law (inertia); second law; mass, weight, normal force, friction; third law.

**Objectives**

- [ ] **N1** Draw a correct free-body diagram for an object and find the net force.
- [ ] **N2** Use Newton's first law to explain the motion of objects with balanced forces, including objects moving at constant velocity.
- [ ] **N3** Apply a = F_net ÷ m to calculate acceleration, net force, or mass, including problems with friction.
- [ ] **N4** Distinguish mass from weight and calculate weight, normal force, and friction force.
- [ ] **N5** Identify Newton's third-law force pairs and explain why they do not cancel.
- [ ] **N6** Analyze lab data to support the claim that acceleration is proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass (HS-PS2-1).

**Checkpoints**

- [ ] Cornell notes complete; every cue answered aloud with the Notes column covered
- [ ] Most-missed quiz at 80% or higher
- [ ] Practice problems completed and checked
- [ ] Lab completed and written up (claim, evidence, reasoning)
- [ ] IXL skills at SmartScore 80+

### Unit 4: Momentum (Weeks 12–14)

*How can we predict what happens in a collision, and how can we make collisions safer?*

**Key concepts:** momentum; impulse; impulse and safety; system; conservation of momentum; collision types.

**Objectives**

- [ ] **M1** Calculate momentum and compare the momenta of different objects, including direction.
- [ ] **M2** Use the impulse–momentum relationship (FΔt = Δp) to find force, time, or change in velocity.
- [ ] **M3** Explain how increasing collision time reduces force, and apply this to the design of a safety device (HS-PS2-3).
- [ ] **M4** Use conservation of momentum to solve one-dimensional collision and explosion problems (HS-PS2-2).
- [ ] **M5** Classify collisions as elastic or inelastic by comparing kinetic energy before and after.

**Checkpoints**

- [ ] Cornell notes complete; every cue answered aloud with the Notes column covered
- [ ] Most-missed quiz at 80% or higher
- [ ] Practice problems completed and checked
- [ ] Lab completed and written up (claim, evidence, reasoning)
- [ ] IXL skills at SmartScore 80+

### Unit 5: Work & Energy (Weeks 15–18)

*Where does energy go when things move, speed up, or stop, and how can we keep track of it?*

**Key concepts:** work; kinetic energy; potential energy; work–energy theorem; conservation of energy; power.

**Objectives**

- [ ] **E1** Calculate the work done by a force and identify when a force does zero work.
- [ ] **E2** Calculate kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy and describe how each changes when speed, mass, or height changes.
- [ ] **E3** Use the work–energy theorem to relate net work to a change in speed.
- [ ] **E4** Apply conservation of energy to find speeds and heights, and account for energy transferred to thermal energy by friction (HS-PS3-1, HS-PS3-2).
- [ ] **E5** Calculate power and compare the power of different energy transfers.
- [ ] **E6** Design, build, and refine a device that converts one form of energy to another within given constraints (HS-PS3-3).

**Checkpoints**

- [ ] Cornell notes complete; every cue answered aloud with the Notes column covered
- [ ] Most-missed quiz at 80% or higher
- [ ] Practice problems completed and checked
- [ ] Lab completed and written up (claim, evidence, reasoning)
- [ ] IXL skills at SmartScore 80+

## How progress is tracked

Each objective is scored on a 4-point proficiency scale (3 = proficient). A unit is mastered when every objective is at level 3 or higher, the most-missed quiz is at 80% or higher, the lab write-up meets the criteria, and the IXL skills are at SmartScore 80+. Full criteria and a blank objective tracker are in [docs/assessment.md](docs/assessment.md).

## Repository layout

```
index.html, notes.html, quiz.html   interactive site (no build step, no dependencies)
assets/                             shared styles and script
data/                               one file per unit: the single source for all content
units/NN-unit/                      generated unit guide, Cornell notes, printable quiz
docs/                               assessment criteria and standards alignment
tools/build.js                      regenerates all Markdown from data/
tools/check.js                      recomputes the numeric answers
```

To change content, edit the unit's file in `data/`, then run `node tools/build.js`.
